chunks: Jameel, from Zurara, from one of them (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Had it not been for my disliking that it would be said, “Muhammad sought support of a group of people, and when he was victorious over his enemy, he killed them,” I would have struck the necks of many people.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad refrain from killing his defeated enemies?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet Muhammad’s (saw) strategic political wisdom and concern for public perception (sira) regarding his treatment of allies. It underscores a key distinction in early Islamic history between temporary military alliances and permanent loyalty, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that his restraint was a calculated measure to preserve the integrity of his leadership rather than mere mercy. This narrative is often cited to illustrate the pragmatic dimensions of the Prophet’s governance during the consolidation of power in Medina.

en.hubeali: H 14991 – Jameel, from Zurara, from one of themasws (Fifth or Sixth Imamasws) having said:

‘The Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Had it not been for my<sup>saww</sup> disliking that they would say, ‘Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> sought support of the people so that he<sup>saww</sup> would be victorious over his<sup>saww</sup> enemies’, I<sup>saww</sup> would have killed a lot of people by striking their necks’.
